title: Pandan Coconut Kaya Toast with Cold Butter and Set Soft Eggs
summary: Pandan-infused coconut cream is cooked gently with eggs and brown sugar into a smooth kaya, spread on crisp toast with cold butter and served with soy-seasoned eggs.
equipment: heatproof bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water

ingredients.item: pandan leaves, cut into 3 cm pieces (or 1/2 tsp pandan flavouring)
fine sea salt or table salt
cold unsalted butter, cut into thin slabs

steps.title: Infuse the pandan
steps.text: Blend the pandan with the coconut cream until the leaves are finely chopped, then press through the sieve and discard the pulp.

steps.title: Cook the kaya
steps.text: Whisk the 2 eggs, sugar and salt in the heatproof bowl until the sugar starts to dissolve, then whisk in the pandan cream. Set the bowl over the barely simmering water and cook, stirring constantly and scraping the sides, for 15-20 minutes, until thick enough to coat the spatula and it reaches 80 °C. Gentle heat stops the eggs scrambling. Sieve it into the jar if it is lumpy and leave to cool; it thickens further as it cools.

steps.title: Cook the eggs
steps.text: Lower the 8 eggs into simmering water in the saucepan and cook for 9 minutes, until the whites are firm and the yolks are just set right through (71 °C). Transfer to the iced water for 1 minute, then peel.

steps.title: Make the toast
steps.text: Toast the bread until golden and crisp, and trim the crusts if you like. Spread 4 slices with about 3 tbsp kaya each, top with slabs of cold butter and close with the other slices. Cut in half.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Halve the eggs into small bowls, season them with the soy sauce and white pepper, and serve with the toast and coffee or tea.

tips: Keep the water barely simmering; if the kaya starts to look grainy, lift the bowl off and whisk hard.
The butter should be fridge-cold so it stays in slabs against the hot toast.
No fresh pandan? Use 1/2 tsp pandan flavouring, stirred in after cooking.
Thin, crisp toast is traditional; thick bread overwhelms the kaya.
storage: Refrigerate kaya in a clean jar and use within 1 week. Toast and eggs are best eaten straight away; refrigerate peeled eggs within 1 hour and use within 2 days. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
